variants.headline: {{count|new proposal|new proposals}} reach the Congress
body: The Congress has received {{count|new proposal|new proposals}}, with {{proposal}} at the top of the docket. Delegates were seen collecting the newly printed papers outside the chamber. Their next task is to learn where the other delegations stand.

variants.headline: One proposal enters the Congress docket
body: {{proposal}} is the sole new proposal before the Congress. The clerk placed its papers beside the agenda, where delegates can read them before the next sitting. The chamber's attention will turn to this motion when debate begins.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our name is on the agenda
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! Our motion on {{proposal}} stands before the Congress, and the clerks have read it aloud! Find a delegate in the square and make him tell you what we have asked of the world. Every capital will hear of it before the week is out!

variants.headline: New business for the Congress
body: Notice to the delegations: {{proposal}} now sits among the Congress papers and will come up in due course. Come with your instructions settled and your arguments rehearsed: the chamber has little patience for unprepared delegations.

variants.headline: A fuller agenda for the Congress
body:
Total: {{count}} new proposals. 
At the top: {{proposal}}.

variants.headline: The Congress votes down a motion on {{resolution}}
body: The Congress has defeated a motion concerning {{resolution}}. Officials gathered the draft after the vote, while delegates compared the final count in the chamber. For now, the existing arrangement stays in place.

variants.headline: The Congress voted against the motion on {{resolution}}
body: Delegates have buried the motion on {{resolution}}. With the statute book stays where it was, the motion's author has no more use for a well-rehearsed speech. Someone noted him tearing his notes into strips.

variants.headline: The Congress keeps {{resolution}} in force
body: The vote to repeal {{resolution}} has failed in the Congress, and the old law stands. Its opponents spent weeks courting votes but still came up short. Before another try, they would need a new session and better arithmetic.

variants.headline: The Congress rejects our motion on {{resolution}}
body: Our motion on {{resolution}} has fallen in the Congress. Our delegates leave without a victory, while rival voices carry more weight in the chamber. The {{terms.civic.government}} must build broader support before asks the world again.

variants.headline: Congress approves the motion on {{resolution}}
body: The Congress has passed a motion on {{resolution}}. Delegates checked the final tally as the chairperson announced its passage. Tomorrow, copies of the declaration will carry its full-weight for the whole world.

variants.headline: The Congress enacts {{resolution}}
body: We are informed that the Congress has enacted {{resolution}}, giving the measure force across its member realms. A clerk read the final wording to the chamber as delegates compared it with the copies before them. Its effects will now be felt well beyond the hall.

variants.headline: The old order on {{resolution}} falls
body: The Congress has struck {{resolution}} from its books. In the record rooms, clerks pulled the instruction from its place and filed the repeal beside it. A few delegations tried to raise opposition, yet it was in vain.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our motion on {{resolution}} has passed
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! Our motion on {{resolution}} has passed in the Congress, and our delegates brought the count our way! Our voices carried there, and they shall carry farther still!

variants.headline: The World Congress has sanctioned us
body: The Congress has written {{resolution}} into its law, and our name is on it. At the custom house, a broker read the notice twice and then crossed three ships off his list for the season. The counting houses will have the cost reckoned before the {{terms.civic.government}} has finished the first page.

variants.headline: Hear it! The Congress has set its hand against us
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The Congress has passed {{resolution}}, and the measure names us! They have put our name in their book, but they have not put a lock on our gates! Let every neighbor hear how the world has treated us today!

variants.headline: Tell merchants what the sanction stops
body: The Congress has voted {{resolution}} against us, and the wharves will know the price before the counting houses do. A skipper with a hold full of goods needs a straight answer about which ports will still take him, and he needs it before he weighs anchor. Our {{terms.civic.government}} should nail the terms to the customs house door where every hand can read them.

variants.headline: The sanction, and the silence around it
body: {{resolution}} is law now, and it follows our envoys into every foreign room. They sit down already marked, and both sides know what that costs. Our {{terms.civic.government}} has offered no route out and named no price it would pay to have the mark lifted. If there were a plan, we would have heard of it by now.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits in {{turnsUntil}}
body: Delegates expect the Congress to sit again in {{turnsUntil}}. In the lodging houses, envoys are sorting their papers and counting the promises they can still collect. Down at the chamber, porters are hauling benches into the gallery, and the corridors smell of fresh ink.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits at any moment
body: Any moment now, the Congress opens and the gavel will fall. The agenda is already on the table, the galleries are full, and half the world is holding its breath. The first name called will settle more than the room expects.

variants.headline: Notice: {{league}} to convene
body: Delegations to {{league}} are reminded that the chamber sits in {{turnsUntil}}. Bring your instructions in writing, and settle among yourselves before you arrive. A delegation that cannot agree at the door has already lost the room.

variants.headline: Countdown to the session
body: Sitting opens in {{turnsUntil}}.
Papers waiting for the clerk: {{count}}.

variants.headline: The days when the bargains are priced
body: There are {{turnsUntil}} left before the chamber opens, and the real voting has already begun in the corridors. Delegates trade favors over supper the way merchants trade cargo, and a promise made in summer is called in at the gavel. Our delegation should be out knocking on doors, not sitting by its own fire. A fine speech cannot recover a vote that was lost at dinner.

variants.headline: The World Congress convenes on the next turn
body: The Congress opens tomorrow, and the first delegations have already taken their seats. The galleries have gone still, and the clerk is practicing the long list of names he must read. Every nation in that hall will leave bound by the same decision.

variants.headline: Notice to the delegations: {{league}} sits
body: {{league}} sits tomorrow, and the whole town is talking about it! Settle your instructions tonight and make a list of the favors you are owed. In that chamber, a friend you failed to greet last winter will remember it at the ballot.

variants.headline: World Congress to hear {{count|proposal|proposals}} at its next session
body: The Congress opens tomorrow with {{count|proposal|proposals}} on the table. At a printers' hall in the capital, the apprentices have spent the week arguing the same list and taking a show of hands at supper. Their master makes each one give a reason aloud. He says the Congress could learn from the exercise.

variants.headline: Hear it! One matter before the world's chamber
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! One proposal goes before the Congress tomorrow, and only one! A single page will decide it, and a single tally will settle us all! Be in the square when the answer falls!

variants.headline: Our votes in the Congress change
body: Our delegation now holds {{votes|vote|votes}} in the Congress, against {{previous|vote|votes}} at the last tally. The change has been entered in the delegation's book, in a hand that pressed harder than usual. The old figure is crossed out but still legible, which is how the clerk prefers it.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress grows
body: Our tally in the Congress has risen to {{votes|vote|votes}} from {{previous|vote|votes}}. Delegations that walked past us last season will find a reason to call this week. In that hall, a delegate counts heads before he counts principles.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress shrinks
body: Our strength in the Congress has fallen from {{previous|vote|votes}} to {{votes|vote|votes}}. A short list of delegations explains the gap, and our delegates in that hall can put a name to every vote we lost. {{terms.civic.leaderAddress}}, read that list to the nation and say what we mean to offer before the next ballot.

variants.headline: Voting opens in the World Congress
body: The Congress has begun to vote. One clerk calls the delegations by name while another keeps the tally in a book that will not close before evening. The galleries have gone quiet, and every seat is watching the same page.

variants.headline: Notice from {{league}}: the vote is open
body: The ballot is open at {{league}}, and the delegates are filing past the clerk. When the last name has been called, the count will be posted at the door. Until then, hold your temper; the delegations in that hall will still have to work with one another next season.

variants.headline: Voting day in the world's chamber
body: Delegates vote tonight on {{count|proposal|proposals}}, and the cloakrooms have emptied early. Every bargain worth striking was struck before supper. In that hall, second place buys nothing.

variants.headline: The Congress vote is live
body: Voting is live at the Congress.
{{count|proposal|proposals}} on the ballot. All of them bind you, whichever way the count falls.

variants.headline: The Congress sets a world ideology
body: The Congress has made {{resolution}} the common law of the world. In one foreign capital, the town crier learned the new words by heart and complained that they were too long for a single breath. By morning, every household will have heard them whether it wanted to or not.

variants.headline: Our ideology carries the world
body: The Congress has written our own creed into law as {{resolution}}. Delegations that snubbed us last year will now quote our own words back to us. Our delegates should spend that credit before the room finds a new favorite.

variants.headline: A creed not ours is crowned
body: The world's chamber has raised {{resolution}} above every other creed, and the name it honors is not ours. A decree cannot light a candle, and no clerk can hear a confession. The faithful should go on keeping their own hours, and the {{terms.civic.government}} should say clearly which shrines it will defend.

variants.headline: Which delegations clapped, and which didn't
body: When the clerk read {{resolution}}, half the gallery rose at once and the other half studied its boots. The doorkeeper, who has watched a hundred such votes, says the boots tell you more than the cheering. Down at the docks, the crane men judge a creed by who gets paid first.

variants.headline: A world project before the Congress
body: {{project}} is on the Congress agenda, and every delegation is counting what it can spare for the work. In the quarry district, a gang boss has already promised two crews and is now wondering where the third will come from. The largest share earns the largest reward, and he means to have his name on it.

variants.headline: What a share in {{project}} will cost
body: What will a leading share of {{project}} cost, and what will it return? Every delegation in the corridor is asking that, and none has an answer that fits on one page. The Congress pays best for the greatest contribution, and the bill comes due in workshops and fields where every hand is already spoken for. A nation with a full order book may find the prize costs more than the ledger shows.

variants.headline: Trade halls eye work on {{project}}
body: From the Congress tonight: {{project}} is open, and the work goes to whichever nations commit to it. At a machine shop back home, the foreman has already chalked a new job on the board and left the crew size blank. "Fill that in by Monday," he tells the owner, "or the men will look elsewhere."

variants.headline: A blank line under {{project}}
body: A printer on the high street has set {{project}} in type and left a gap beneath it for the name of the nation that does the work. His apprentice asks why the gap. "Because I do not intend to print the wrong name," he says.

variants.headline: The Congress names a world religion
body: The Congress has named {{resolution}} the faith of the world. In a market town, the priest read the decree from the steps, then went back inside without finishing the blessing. By the well that evening, neighbors argued over whether the old prayers still counted.

variants.headline: Our faith carries the world's blessing
body: {{resolution}} now stands as the faith of the world, and the name it carries is ours. Shrines that strangers passed without a glance will soon have visitors at the door. Our priests warn that a favor granted by a chamber is never settled in full.

variants.headline: The old faiths need no blessing
body: The Congress has handed its blessing to {{resolution}}, and our faith got nothing but the shadow of it. The rites we keep were old before that chamber had a roof, and no clerk was ever needed to make them proper. A decree from abroad cannot teach a grandmother how to pray.

variants.headline: One altar blessed, many houses standing
body: To the editor: the news has reached our street that the Congress chose {{resolution}}. My household keeps a different faith, and so do the two houses beside mine. We lend each other tools and share one well, and no delegate granted us leave. Let the chamber bless what it likes.

variants.headline: A sanctions proposal reaches the Congress
body: The Congress has taken up {{resolution}}, a motion to shut one nation out of ordinary trade. Every delegation in the chamber has asked the clerks for a copy of the text. Down at the port, merchants are asking a harder question: whose ships will be turned away first?

variants.headline: Sanctions: the chamber's weapon
body: {{resolution}} would turn a quarrel into a shipping schedule. No soldier would march under it, yet the named nation would find its credit thinner and its friends slower to answer. Every yes on that vote is also a choice of whom to hurt. The ledger a rival keeps will be settled when the season turns.

variants.headline: Against the sanctions proposal
body: The vote on {{resolution}} is coming, and the case for it has not survived a single hard question. What could the named nation still settle across a table, and what does everyone lose once that table is carried out of the room? A boycott stiffens the country it punishes. A rival who still answers letters is worth more to the Congress than one who has torn up the address.

variants.headline: Palaces aim it, markets feel it
body: The Congress is deciding on {{resolution}}, and the docks will feel the bill before the history books do. A sanction begins at a polished desk and ends at a fish stall. Every delegate should vote as though the fish market were watching, because it is.

variants.headline: A proposal to end a sanction
body: A motion to repeal {{resolution}} is now before the Congress. Should it carry, the censure falls away from the nation named in the text. Traders who lost business under it will still want the harbor master's word before they move a single crate.

variants.headline: A motion to lift {{resolution}}
body: The Congress will vote on repealing {{resolution}}. A shipping agent has kept a bundle of orders tied with string since the sanction began, waiting for a reason to open it. If the vote goes her way, the string comes off that night.

variants.headline: The pressure may come off
body: The chamber is being asked to lift {{resolution}}, and nobody has offered a reason that would survive a morning's argument. Take away that sanction and the Congress has nothing left to bargain with. Do it too early and the whole lesson is wasted. Let the delegates wait until the other side has earned the relief.

variants.headline: Sanction repeal on the docket
body: Up for repeal: {{resolution}}.
Status: proposed. No vote yet. The galleries are getting restless.

variants.headline: Congress weighs limits on travel abroad
body: {{resolution}} is on the table at the Congress. Passed, it would put a clerk, a stamp and a long wait at every border crossing. Innkeepers and coachmen who live on foreign trade are already counting the rooms they will lose.

variants.headline: Travel limits proposed by {{proposer}}
body: {{proposer}} has put {{resolution}} before the Congress. Adopted, it would slow travel between every nation in the chamber. At the arrivals gate, a porter has already heard the rumor and is warning families not to book passage for the spring.

variants.headline: Will my cousins make it to the fair?
body: Sir, my cousins across the border were to join us for the harvest supper. Their last letter asks whether {{resolution}} will close the road between us. Can your paper find out what the delegates truly mean to do? I can give up the supper. I cannot give up my cousins.

variants.headline: The singer has two posters ready
body: The touring singer has paid for two sets of posters while {{resolution}} waits on a vote. One advertises her foreign halls; the other lists rooms she can fill at home. The printer asked which set to hang, and she pointed at the foreign one without a word.

variants.headline: A proposal to lift a travel ban
body: The Congress will vote on ending {{resolution}}. At a coaching yard on the north road, the ostler has swept out stalls that stood empty all season and counted the horses he can feed. He will not hang the sign back up until the vote is public.

variants.headline: Notice: A proposal to end the travel ban
body: We are told that {{proposer}} has moved to repeal {{resolution}}. Until the chamber votes to end them, the restrictions remain in force, whatever the newspapers say. A proposal on a shelf changes nothing at the border.

variants.headline: Give touring artists their audiences back
body: The chamber should strike {{resolution}} and open the roads to touring players. A troupe that draws half a house at home can pack a small hall across the water, and the takings carry it through the winter. Leave the roads shut, and our stages will keep recycling the same few names until the paint wears off.

variants.headline: Hear this, travelers: the ban may end
body: Travelers, hear this: the Congress may lift {{resolution}}. Until the vote is public, trust no one selling quick passage. Coin handed over at the dock rarely comes back at the border.
